sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Pre-Independence Vision (1934-1944)**: Genesis began with M. Visvesvaraya's **Planned Economy for India (1934)**, followed by the **National Planning Committee (1938)** under Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, the capitalist **Bombay Plan (1944)**, Gandhian **Gandhian Plan (1944)** by S.N. Agarwal, and M.N. Roy's socialist **People's Plan (1945)**.
• **Post-Independence Institutional Genesis**: The **Planning Commission** was established on March 15, 1950, through a Cabinet Resolution (non-statutory, extra-constitutional body) with the Prime Minister as its ex-officio Chairman.
• **National Development Council (NDC)**: Established on August 6, 1952, to secure cooperation of states in execution of plans and strengthen federal planning.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Transition from centralised command planning (First to Twelfth Five Year Plans) to decentralised, think-tank driven cooperative federalism via **NITI Aayog (January 1, 2015)**.

items.definition: Adopted significantly from the Eighth Plan onwards; the state sets broad targets and guides the private sector through incentives rather than mandatory physical controls.
Command economy planning where targets, resource allocation, and production quotas are rigidly fixed by the central authority (resembled early Soviet-style pre-1991 Indian socialist leanings).
The approved criteria used since the Fourth Plan to allocate central assistance for state plans among various states, based on population, tax effort, per capita income, and special problems.
National Planning Committee (1938), Bombay Plan (1944), Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) reports, and the 2014 Aayog restructuring cabinet resolution.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Public Sector Industrial Belts**: Heavy engineering hubs established in Chota Nagpur Plateau (Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Durgapur, Bhilai) leveraging rich mineral and coal reserves.
• **Green Revolution Epicenters**: Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh targeted via intensive agricultural planning during the late 1960s.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Top-down rigidities, regional disparities, sluggish employment generation, and fiscal federalism friction.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift to NITI Aayog's bottom-up approach, competitive and cooperative federalism, Aspirational Districts Programme, and SDG India Index.

items.title: Mnemonic for Pre-Independence Plans Chronology
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **V**isvesvaraya **N**ational **B**ombay **G**andhian **P**eople
• **Decoded Meaning**: Visvesvaraya Plan (1934) -> National Planning Committee (1938) -> Bombay Plan (1944) -> Gandhian Plan (1944) -> People's Plan (1945).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly sorts chronological arrangement questions in Prelims.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Models remember: 1st Plan = Harrod-Domar (Agriculture/Short term), 2nd Plan = Mahalanobis (Heavy Industry/Long term).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the Planning Commission or National Development Council are statutory or constitutional bodies. Both were extra-constitutional and non-statutory bodies created via executive resolutions.

Mains Value Addition: Critically evaluate the transition from 'Centralized Planning' to 'Policy Think Tank (NITI Aayog)' using keywords like fiscal federalism, bottom-up planning, and competitive federalism.

keyTakeaways: Indian planning evolved from nationalist private blueprints (Bombay Plan) into a centralized state-led economic model post-independence.
The First and Second Five Year Plans laid the dual foundations of agricultural security and heavy industrialization.
The abolition of the Planning Commission and setting up of NITI Aayog marked the historic shift from command planning to cooperative federalism.
